title: ORBIT-Surgical: An Open-Simulation Framework for Learning Surgical Augmented Dexterity

metadata.authors: Yu, Qinxi; Moghani, Masoud; Dharmarajan, Karthik; Schorp, Vincent; Panitch, William Chung-Ho; Liu, Jingzhou; Hari, Kush; Huang, Huang; Mittal, Mayank; Goldberg, Ken; Garg, Animesh

source_summary: ORBIT-Surgical is a physics-based surgical robot simulation framework with photorealistic rendering that enables reinforcement and imitation learning for surgical tasks, provides benchmarks for dVRK and STAR robots, supports realistic data generation, and demonstrates sim-to-real policy transfer.
abstract: Physics-based simulations have accelerated progress in robot learning for driving, manipulation, and locomotion. Yet, a fast, accurate, and robust surgical simulation environment remains a challenge. In this paper, we present ORBIT-Surgical, a physics-based surgical robot simulation framework with photorealistic rendering in NVIDIA Omniverse. We provide 14 benchmark surgical tasks for the da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) and Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot (STAR) which represent common subtasks in surgical training. ORBIT-Surgical leverages GPU parallelization to train reinforcement learning and imitation learning algorithms to facilitate study of robot learning to augment human surgical skills. ORBIT-Surgical also facilitates realistic synthetic data generation for active perception tasks. We demonstrate ORBIT-Surgical sim-to-real transfer of learned policies onto a physical dVRK robot. Project website: orbit-surgical.github.io

methods.value: Creation of ORBIT-Surgical, a simulation framework based on NVIDIA Isaac Sim, providing GPU-accelerated physics, contact-rich physical interactions, and high-fidelity rendering.

problems.value: Developing a fast, accurate, and robust surgical simulation environment for robot learning.

hypotheses.value: A physics-based surgical robot simulation framework with photorealistic rendering can facilitate study of robot learning to augment human surgical skills.

evidence.value: Successful sim-to-real transfer of learned policies onto a physical dVRK robot, high learning speed facilitated by ORBIT-Surgical, and improved perception performance by over 2× using synthetic data generation.

conclusions.value: ORBIT-Surgical enables efficient training of reinforcement learning policies for surgical robotics tasks and high-fidelity synthetic data generation, accelerating progress in learning-based assistive autonomy in robotic surgery.
